questions.question: Which statement is true about JDK?

options.D: Contains JRE, JVM, and development tools

questions.correct_answer: D. Contains JRE, JVM, and development tools
questions.explanation: JDK = JRE (which includes JVM) + development tools such as javac.

questions.question: Why is Java called platform independent?

options.A: Java code is interpreted directly by OS
options.B: Bytecode can run on any JVM

questions.correct_answer: B. Bytecode can run on any JVM
questions.explanation: Source compiles to bytecode, which runs on any platform having a JVM (WORA).

questions.explanation: && and || skip the right operand when the result is already known; & doesn't.

questions.question: Which member belongs to the class rather than an object?
questions.explanation: Static members belong to the class.

questions.question: Can two methods have the same name?
questions.explanation: Methods with the same name but different parameter lists are overloaded.

questions.question: Which access modifier gives the widest accessibility?
questions.explanation: public is accessible from everywhere.

questions.question: Which access modifier restricts access within the same class only?
questions.explanation: private is limited to the declaring class.

questions.explanation: return ends method execution and returns to the caller.

options.A: Package names must start with capital letters

questions.correct_answer: B. Packages help avoid naming conflicts
questions.explanation: Packages namespace classes, avoiding name clashes and organising code.

options.C: Run till next breakpoint or program completion

questions.question: An inventory system stores 10,000 product IDs in an array. Which characteristic of arrays allows quick retrieval of any element using its index?

options.B: Elements are stored in contiguous memory locations.
options.D: Arrays store data in Method Area.

questions.correct_answer: B. Elements are stored in contiguous memory locations.
questions.explanation: Contiguous storage gives O(1) access: address = base + index × size.

questions.question: If arrays require contiguous memory, what happens when we need a larger array?

options.A: JVM automatically increases the same memory block.
options.B: A new larger array is created and data is copied.

questions.correct_answer: B. A new larger array is created and data is copied.
questions.explanation: Array size is fixed, so you allocate a bigger array and copy elements over.

questions.question: When should a for loop be preferred over a while loop?

options.A: When the number of iterations is unknown
options.D: When the number of iterations is known in advance

questions.correct_answer: D. When the number of iterations is known in advance
questions.explanation: for bundles init, condition and update, which suits a known iteration count.

questions.question: Which loop is generally preferred for reading user input until the user enters a specific value?
questions.explanation: The iteration count is unknown, so a condition-driven while loop fits.
With no condition, for(;;) runs forever.

questions.question: Which statement is TRUE?

options.A: for loop cannot become an infinite loop.
options.B: while loop cannot become an infinite loop.
options.C: Both for and while can become infinite loops.
options.D: Neither can become an infinite loop.

questions.correct_answer: C. Both for and while can become infinite loops.
questions.explanation: Any loop whose condition never becomes false (or is omitted) runs forever.

questions.question: An ATM application keeps asking for a PIN until the correct PIN is entered. Which loop is more suitable?
questions.explanation: The number of attempts is unknown, so a condition-based loop fits.

questions.question: An inventory system needs to scan exactly 500 products. Which loop should be preferred?

options.A: while loop because it is faster
options.B: for loop because the number of iterations is known

questions.correct_answer: B. for loop because the number of iterations is known
questions.explanation: A known iteration count suits for; speed is not the reason.

questions.question: An inventory system needs to scan exactly 500 products. Which loop should be preferred? (duplicate)

options.A: while loop because it is faster
options.B: for loop because the number of iterations is known

questions.correct_answer: B. for loop because the number of iterations is known
questions.explanation: Same as Q37: use for when the iteration count is known.

questions.question: Which statement about this() and super() is correct?

options.A: Both can be used together in the same constructor
options.B: this() must always be the last statement
options.C: this() or super() must be the first statement of a constructor
options.D: super() can be called from any method

questions.correct_answer: C. this() or super() must be the first statement of a constructor
questions.explanation: A constructor call must be the first statement, and only one of the two can be used.
